name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (battle AoE/tile domain). 'mark_aoe_plus_pattern_at' accurately describes the behavior: mark a '+' (plus) shaped 5-tile AoE pattern at a given (x,y). No Ghidra address residue in the name; '_at' is the idiomatic position-taking suffix, not a hex remnant.
purpose: Mark a '+' shaped 5-tile AoE/threat overlay pattern centered at (x,y) on the battle tile map: center tile gets overlay bit 0x40, the four cardinal neighbors get bit 0x80.
logic_summary: For each of the 4 cardinal neighbors (left, up, right, down) it first bounds-checks the edge (x!=0; y!=0; x<width-1; y<height-1) and, if in-bounds, calls fd2_set_tile_overlay_bit_80 to OR bit 0x80 into that neighbor's overlay byte (tile stride 4, overlay byte at +6). Finally it ORs bit 0x40 into the center tile's overlay byte at (x + y*width)*4 + 6. Center marker bit 0x40 distinguishes the primary/center tile from the 0x80 splash neighbors. (Watcom __CHK(0x14) stack-probe in the binary is elided in the rebuilt C source per project convention.)

params.name: x
params.semantics: Tile column (world x) of the center of the '+' pattern. Compared signed against width-1 for the right-neighbor bound; used in the center index (x + y*width)*4 + 6.
params.reason: Accurate, concise, no address residue; matches caller (passes runtime_char[char_idx].bPos_x).

params.name: y
params.semantics: Tile row (world y) of the center of the '+' pattern. Compared signed against height-1 for the down-neighbor bound; used in the center index (x + y*width)*4 + 6.
params.reason: Accurate, concise, no address residue; matches caller (passes runtime_char[char_idx].bPos_y).

returns.semantics: No return value; effect is mutation of the battle tile map overlay bytes in place.

notes: Single caller: fd2_paint_threat_overlay_for_team @ 0x145cd (calls per alive char of selected team to render the threat/AoE-coverage overlay during action target selection). Disassembly @ 0x14625 confirms: EBX=x, ESI=y, neighbor calls to 0x146a7 (fd2_set_tile_overlay_bit_80), width [0x53ac1] and height [0x53ac5] decremented for bounds, center OR 0x40 at tile_map_ptr [0x53a51] + (x+y*width)*4 + 6. Source C comment (lines 259-264) and Ghidra plate are both accurate and mutually consistent, so neither was changed. NOTE: writes_globals lists data_fd2_battle_tile_map_ptr because the function writes through the buffer it points to (the pointer value itself is not modified).
